statement: Which number is made of 3 thousands, 14 hundreds, 5 tens and 12 ones?

choices.misconception: I treated 14 hundreds as 140, mixing up hundreds and tens.
I wrote 4 in the hundreds place for the 14 hundreds and dropped the extra thousand.
I added 5 for the 5 tens instead of 50.
I wrote 2 in the ones place for the 12 ones and dropped the extra ten.

hints: Turn each part into an ordinary number before adding.
Some parts have more than 9 of a kind, so they spill over into the next place. Write each part as a plain number, then add them all.
14 hundreds is 1400 and 12 ones is 12. Add 3000, 1400, 50 and 12.

solutions.reliable: 3 thousands is 3000, 14 hundreds is 1400, 5 tens is 50 and 12 ones is 12. Adding: 3000 + 1400 + 50 + 12 = 4462. The transferable idea: when a place holds 10 or more, regroup it into the next place up before writing the digits.
solutions.elegant: Regroup first: 14 hundreds is 1 thousand and 4 hundreds, and 12 ones is 1 ten and 2 ones. That makes 4 thousands, 4 hundreds, 6 tens and 2 ones: 4462.

whyOnTest: Places holding more than 9 test whether you understand regrouping, not just reading digits off in order.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
